verdict.rationale: Drata offers a public API and an MCP server, so a separate sandbox or test environment is a fair thing to ask about, but nothing in the evidence documents one or any way to test without touching production data. Community suggestions to isolate the Drata agent in a VM or on a dedicated laptop are user-side workarounds and earn no credit. The 'Monitoring Tests' endpoints are compliance control tests, not a sandbox for trying out integrations.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data
